memos.headline: Broad Momentum Surge Leaves Most Names Overbought; S07 and S08 Offer Best Risk-Adjusted Trend Setups
memos.body: I see a market where nearly everything has rallied hard over the past four weeks, pushing RSIs into the 70s across multiple names. S07 stands out as the strongest trend in the universe—sitting at its 52-week high with +23.1% over 12 weeks and +19.5% relative strength vs SPY over that period—yet its RSI at 64.5 is not yet extreme, giving room to run. S08 is my second-favorite setup: above both moving averages with a moderate RSI of 64.2, only -5.6% off highs, and consistent positive relative strength (+5.5% vs SPY over 12 weeks). I am cautious on the sharp mean-reversion bounces in S04 and S02, which are still deeply below their 200-day means and 52-week highs despite eye-catching weekly returns—these look like bear-market rallies until proven otherwise. S09 is the weakest name on a short-term basis with RSI 36.5 and -15% relative strength over 4 weeks, and I would avoid it until it reclaims its 50-day average.

views.note: At 52-week highs with +39.5% above 200d mean and RSI 64.5 not yet extreme; would reassess on a close below 730 (~8% pullback to near 50d area).
Healthy uptrend above both moving averages, RSI 64.2, only -5.6% off highs with steady relative strength; would exit on a break below the 200d mean (~252 area).
Strong 4w +12.9% rally and +6.4% 12w relative strength, but RSI 71.4 and +10% above 50d mean suggest near-term pullback risk; would trim on a break below 190.
RSI 76.6 is the highest in the universe and +17% above 50d mean screams overextension despite the powerful trend; waiting for a pullback toward the 50d before adding.
Near 52-week highs and +25.4% above 200d mean with RSI 72.6; trend is strong but 12w relative strength vs SPY is only +0.4%, suggesting momentum is fading relative to the market.
Still -22% off highs and -10.4% below 200d mean despite a +14% weekly spike; this looks like a bear-market bounce and I need a close above 460 to reconsider.
A staggering -44.5% drawdown from 52-week highs with 12w relative strength of -10.3% vs SPY; the sharp bounce has pushed RSI to 73 but the intermediate trend is clearly broken.
RSI 36.5 and -5.3% below 50d mean with -15% 4w relative strength; high ATR of 4.26% adds risk—need a reclaim of the 50d average (~154) to turn constructive.
Middling setup: above both averages but only +0.1% 4w relative strength vs SPY and -7.3% off highs; no edge either way until it breaks above 320 or below 295.
Below both 50d and 200d means, -13.9% off highs, and negative relative strength on all timeframes; would need a close above 155 to reconsider.

memos.headline: S10 and S04 Show Exceptional Earnings Power; S02 and S09 Flash Red on Margin Collapse
memos.body: I see a stark bifurcation in this universe between durable, high-margin compounders and names where earnings power is deteriorating fast. S10 stands out with 63.1% net margins, 73.2% YoY revenue growth, and near-doubling of net income on only $8.47B of total debt — this is the cleanest fundamental profile in the group. S04 is similarly compelling at 47.3% net margins with net income up 59.5% YoY, though its $40.26B debt load warrants monitoring. On the other end, S02 posted a near-total earnings wipeout — net income collapsed 99.8% YoY to essentially zero on $113.22B of revenue, with $78.39B in debt, which is a clear avoid until margins recover. S09 also concerns me: revenue declined 1.3% while net income fell 14.6% on a thin 7.9% margin, suggesting operating leverage is working against it. I would need to see margin stabilization in S02 and S09 before reconsidering.

views.note: 63.1% net margin, 73.2% revenue growth, 94.5% net income growth, and minimal debt of $8.47B make this the strongest fundamental story in the universe.
47.3% net margin and 59.5% net income growth demonstrate exceptional earnings power; would reassess if margins compress below 40%.
Solid 30.3% net margin, 18% revenue growth, 29.8% net income growth, and low debt of $14.79B support a durable earnings profile.
Revenue of $143.76B and 29.3% net margin are healthy, but $88.50B in total debt and moderating growth of 15.7% temper enthusiasm.
Revenue growth of 13.6% is decent but net margin of only 9.9% and net income growth of just 5.9% suggest limited earnings leverage.
28.4% net margin is respectable but net income declined 7% YoY and $435.21B in total debt (likely a financial) introduces significant balance-sheet risk.
19.4% net margin is adequate but revenue grew only 1.5% and net income fell 6.7%, signaling stagnation; need to see top-line reacceleration.
18% revenue growth is encouraging but net income fell 13.9% and 12.5% margin with $36.21B debt suggests margin pressure is real.
Revenue declining 1.3% with net income down 14.6% on a thin 7.9% margin and $34.24B debt signals deteriorating earnings power.
Net income collapsed 99.8% YoY to near zero on $113B revenue with $78.39B debt — earnings power is effectively gone until margin recovery is demonstrated.

memos.headline: Fed on Pause at 3.75% With Sticky 3.3% CPI — Favor Banks and Staples Over Duration-Sensitive Growth
memos.body: I see the Fed firmly in a pause regime: the upper bound has been flat at 3.75% for three months after 75 bps of cuts over the past year, and CPI running at 3.3% YoY gives the FOMC little room to ease further. The labor market is stable with unemployment at 4.3%, down 10 bps over the last quarter, which removes any urgency to cut. The 10y-2y spread has narrowed 11 bps over three months to +0.54 pp, suggesting the long end is pricing in slower growth or a prolonged pause rather than further easing — this is a headwind for pure duration plays. I have moderate conviction that this pause-with-sticky-inflation backdrop favors banks (positive curve, stable credit) and defensive staples, while duration-sensitive growth names face valuation pressure from a 4.26% 10y yield. A CPI print dropping below 2.8% or unemployment rising above 4.5% would shift my regime call toward renewed easing.

views.note: Banks benefit from a positively sloped curve at +54 bps and a stable labor market keeping credit losses contained.
Staples offer defensive positioning in a pause regime where sticky 3.3% inflation supports pricing power without triggering recession fears.
Duration-sensitive growth faces headwinds from a 4.26% 10y yield and no near-term catalyst for further rate cuts.
High-duration tech/growth names are vulnerable if the pause extends and the 10y yield stays above 4.2%.
Cyclicals face mixed signals — stable employment supports demand but the narrowing curve and sticky inflation limit upside.
Energy is macro-neutral here; no clear directional signal from the rate or growth data alone.

memos.headline: S05 Leadership Churn and S10 Post-Earnings Negativity Stand Out; S03 Filing Cadence Signals Active Narrative
memos.body: I am reading the 8-K filing cadence and event types across the universe as a proxy for media-relevant narrative shifts, since no GDELT tone data was provided directly. S03 has filed six 8-Ks since late February—including a material definitive agreement and multiple Reg FD disclosures through April 14—suggesting an accelerating corporate narrative that could attract positive coverage momentum. S05 has filed three consecutive Departure/Appointment of Directors or Officers 8-Ks in roughly five weeks, which I read as leadership instability that typically generates negative sentiment drift. S10 posted a -5.5% price reaction on its Feb 25 earnings release and followed up with a board change on Mar 6; that combination usually keeps tone depressed for weeks and I see no catalyst to reverse it. S06 reported results on Apr 14 with only a -0.8% move, suggesting the negative tone was already priced, and the simultaneous Reg FD filing hints at forward guidance that could shift sentiment modestly positive.

views.note: Unusually high filing cadence including a material agreement and repeated Reg FD disclosures suggests a building positive narrative.
Three director/officer departure filings in five weeks signals leadership instability likely to weigh on sentiment.
Sharp -5.5% earnings reaction in February followed by a board change with no positive catalyst suggests lingering negative tone.
Muted -0.8% reaction to earnings implies negative sentiment was already priced; paired Reg FD disclosure could nudge tone upward but conviction is low.
Mixed signals from an officer change and two Other Events filings; not enough directional tone shift to take a view.
Two officer-change filings and a Reg FD disclosure are routine; no clear sentiment inflection.

memos.headline: Surging Oil Prices and Elevated Policy Uncertainty Signal Geopolitical Supply-Chain Stress Across the Universe
memos.body: I am focused on the 62.4% three-month surge in WTI to $96.46/bbl, which is the clearest geopolitical signal in the data and points to either supply disruption or sanctions-driven tightening—this is a structural shift until proven otherwise. The Economic Policy Uncertainty Index at 262.82, up 8.1% month-over-month and 2.1% over three months, confirms that policy risk remains elevated even as VIX has pulled back 23.7% over the past month, suggesting equity vol is under-pricing the policy backdrop. HY OAS at 2.86% has tightened 41bp over the month but is still 21bp wider over three months, consistent with credit markets partially digesting but not fully clearing the geopolitical overhang. S03 stands out with five 8-K filings since late February—an unusually high cadence of Reg FD and Other Events disclosures that may reflect operational or regulatory developments tied to the current environment. I would need clarity on whether the oil move reflects Iran/Russia sanctions escalation or OPEC supply management before upgrading conviction on energy-exposed names.

views.note: Unusually high 8-K filing frequency (five since Feb-27) warrants monitoring but without disclosure detail I cannot take a directional view; a sanctions-related catalyst would shift me to avoid.
Two recent 8-Ks and the sharp oil price move suggest potential energy-security or supply-chain exposure; staying neutral pending detail on whether filings relate to geopolitical contingencies.
Reg FD filings in Feb and Apr bracket the period of rising policy uncertainty; without content I lean neutral but would avoid if export-control exposure is confirmed.
Single Reg FD filing on Apr-14 coincides with peak policy uncertainty; no basis for directional call but the macro backdrop warrants caution.
Two 8-Ks in the period and the VIX pullback suggest the market may be discounting near-term risk; if S07 has domestic-oriented revenue it could benefit from easing vol even as oil stays elevated.
Only one Reg FD filing back in March and the combination of $96 oil and 263-level policy uncertainty raises input-cost and regulatory risk for names without recent disclosure updates.
